row.evidence: PayPal's help centre describes only manual secondary-user management ("give PayPal account access to up to 200 employees, each with a unique login ID"), and no PayPal page documents SCIM or SAML SSO for business accounts; Okta's PayPal app is SWA-only.
row.notes: New row, scored on the PayPal business account (merchant account with secondary users). No SCIM or SAML SSO documented: the US help-centre sitemap, the fees page and the full developer.paypal.com docs index were searched; the only SCIM in PayPal's docs is for Braintree (separate row, gated). Up to 200 secondary users are managed by hand by the primary owner; a User Audit report is available in the reporting portal. Pricing is per transaction (PayPal Checkout 3.49% + fixed fee), so plan and per-user fields are null. Okta's "PayPal" app is SWA; "PayPal IdP" is Log in with PayPal as an inbound identity source, unrelated to provisioning.

plans.name: PayPal Business account (standard rates)
plans.price_text: PayPal Checkout 3.49% + fixed fee per transaction
plans.notes: Transaction-priced; no per-user tiers. Optional gateway products carry monthly fees (Payments Advanced $5, Payments Pro $30).

scim.notes: No SCIM documented for PayPal business accounts: the developer docs index (all sections) mentions SCIM only for Braintree, which has its own row (slug braintree). Left null (PayPal never says no); status none by absence.

audit_log_api.notes: User Audit report (user actions, logins) is available as a report in the PayPal reporting portal, not documented as an API.

user_api.notes: The PayPal REST/NVP API catalogue covers payments, orders, invoicing, disputes, payouts and reports; no endpoints for managing secondary users of a business account were found. The "Identity" API is Log in with PayPal (customer identity), not admin user management.

okta.notes: OIN markup checks only SWA for "PayPal" (and "PayPal Manager"). "PayPal IdP" (Inbound Federation, SCIM, Attribute Sourcing) is Log in with PayPal as an identity source into Okta, not provisioning into a PayPal business account.

entra.notes: No PayPal entry in the Entra SaaS tutorial index (learn.microsoft.com toc.json).

fallbacks.notes: Secondary users (up to 200) are added, permissioned and deleted manually by the primary account owner under Account Settings > Manage users.
